sections.title: Review: 2D Shapes

learn.title: Unit 7 in one look
learn.html:
🔺 Equilateral: 3 equal sides, 3 angles of 60°.

🔺 Isosceles: 2 equal sides, 2 equal base angles.

📐 Angles in a triangle add up to 180°.

⭕ Radius = diameter ÷ 2. A compass is set to the radius.

questions.label: Review 1 (a)
questions.q: Tick (✓) the correct properties of triangles, and cross (✗) the wrong ones. (a) All sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.
questions.hint: Think about what each type of triangle looks like. Draw one if it helps.
steps: An isosceles triangle has only 2 equal sides. (All 3 sides equal is an equilateral triangle.)
questions.why: An isosceles triangle has only 2 equal sides. (All 3 sides equal is an equilateral triangle.)

questions.label: Review 1 (b)
questions.q: Tick (✓) the correct properties of triangles, and cross (✗) the wrong ones. (b) Interior angles of an equilateral triangle are equal.
questions.hint: Think about what each type of triangle looks like. Draw one if it helps.
steps: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles: 180° ÷ 3 = 60° each.
questions.why: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles: 180° ÷ 3 = 60° each.

questions.label: Review 1 (c)
questions.q: Tick (✓) the correct properties of triangles, and cross (✗) the wrong ones. (c) An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides.
questions.hint: Think about what each type of triangle looks like. Draw one if it helps.
steps: Yes. An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides.
questions.why: Yes. An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides.

questions.label: Review 1 (d)
questions.q: Tick (✓) the correct properties of triangles, and cross (✗) the wrong ones. (d) Interior angles of an obtuse triangle are all obtuse.
questions.hint: Think about what each type of triangle looks like. Draw one if it helps.
steps: An obtuse triangle has only 1 obtuse angle. The other 2 angles are acute. (3 obtuse angles would be more than 180°.)
questions.why: An obtuse triangle has only 1 obtuse angle. The other 2 angles are acute. (3 obtuse angles would be more than 180°.)

questions.label: Review 1 (e)
questions.q: Tick (✓) the correct properties of triangles, and cross (✗) the wrong ones. (e) There is 1 right angle inside a right triangle.
questions.hint: Think about what each type of triangle looks like. Draw one if it helps.
steps: Yes. A right triangle has exactly 1 right angle (90°).
questions.why: Yes. A right triangle has exactly 1 right angle (90°).

questions.label: Review 2 (a)
questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) ABC is an equilateral triangle. ∠BAC = ___°, ∠ABC = ___°, AB = ___ cm, AC = ___ cm
questions.hint: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles.
steps: All 3 angles are equal and add up to 180°.
All 3 sides are equal. CB = 10 cm, so AB = 10 cm and AC = 10 cm.
questions.why: Equilateral: all angles 60° and all sides equal (10 cm).

questions.label: Review 2 (b)
questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (b) DEF is an isosceles triangle. ∠DEF = ___°, DE = ___ cm
questions.hint: The 2 base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. The 2 equal sides are DE and DF.
steps: The angles add up to 180°. Take away the top angle: 180° - 40° = 140°.
The 2 base angles are equal: 140° ÷ 2 = 70°. So ∠DEF = 70°.
DE and DF are the equal sides. DF = 12 cm, so DE = 12 cm.

questions.label: Review 2 (c)
questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (c) JKL is a right triangle. ∠JKL = ___°, ∠JLK = ___°, ∠JLK + ∠KJL = ___°
questions.hint: The little square at K means a right angle (90°). All 3 angles add up to 180°.
steps: The little square at K shows ∠JKL = 90°.

questions.label: Review 3 (a)
questions.q: Find each unknown angle. (a)
questions.hint: Look at the tick marks. Equal sides mean equal angles. Angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
steps: All 3 sides have a tick mark, so they are all equal. It is an equilateral triangle.
questions.why: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal angles: 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

questions.label: Review 3 (b)
questions.q: Find each unknown angle. (b)
questions.hint: Look at the tick marks. Equal sides mean equal angles. Angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
steps: The 2 sides with tick marks are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. Its 2 base angles are equal.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. Take away the top angle: 180° - 70° = 110°
Share it between the 2 equal angles: 110° ÷ 2 = 55°

questions.label: Review 3 (c)
questions.q: Find each unknown angle. (c)
questions.hint: Look at the tick marks. Equal sides mean equal angles. Angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
steps: The 2 sides with tick marks are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. Its 2 base angles are equal.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. Take away the top angle: 180° - 24° = 156°
Share it between the 2 equal angles: 156° ÷ 2 = 78°

questions.label: Review 3 (d)
questions.q: Find each unknown angle. (d)
questions.hint: Look at the tick marks. Equal sides mean equal angles. Angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
steps: The 2 sides with tick marks are equal, so it is an isosceles triangle. Its 2 base angles are equal.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. Take away the top angle: 180° - 110° = 70°
Share it between the 2 equal angles: 70° ÷ 2 = 35°

questions.label: Review 4 (a)
questions.q: Draw the following triangles. (a) Draw a triangle ABC in which ∠ACB = 90° and AC and CB = 5 cm.
questions.hint: Draw CB first. Then make a right angle at C with a protractor or a set square.
steps: Use a ruler. Draw a line CB that is 5 cm long.
At C, use a protractor (or set square) to draw a line going straight up: 90°.
Measure 5 cm up this line and mark A.
Join A to B with the ruler.
Check: AB is about 7 cm long.
questions.answer: Triangle ABC with a right angle at C, AC = 5 cm and CB = 5 cm (like the picture).
questions.why: Two sides of 5 cm with a 90° angle between them make a right isosceles triangle.

questions.label: Review 4 (b)
questions.q: Draw the following triangles. (b) Draw a triangle EFG in which EF and EG = 5 cm and GF = 4 cm.
questions.hint: Draw GF first. Then use a compass set to 5 cm from G and from F.
steps: Use a ruler. Draw a line GF that is 4 cm long.
Put the needle on G and draw an arc above the line.
Put the needle on F and draw another arc. The arcs cross at E.
Join E to G and E to F. EG = EF = 5 cm.
questions.answer: Triangle EFG with EF = EG = 5 cm and GF = 4 cm (like the picture).
questions.why: Arcs of 5 cm from G and from F meet at E, so EG and EF are both 5 cm.

questions.label: Review 5
questions.q: Complete the diagram with parts of a circle.
questions.hint: Use the words: center, radius, diameter, chord, circumference.
steps: A line from the center to the edge is a radius.
A line across the circle through the center is a diameter. (It is also a chord.)
A line joining 2 points on the edge, not through the center, is a chord.
The curved line all the way round is the circumference.
questions.answer: Center, Radius, Diameter/Chord, Chord, Circumference (as labelled in the picture).
questions.why: A diameter goes through the center; a chord does not have to.

questions.label: Review 6
questions.q: Draw a circle J in which its diameter = 4 cm.
questions.hint: A compass is set to the radius. Radius = diameter ÷ 2.
steps: Open the compass to 2 cm with a ruler.
Put the needle on J and turn the compass all the way round.
questions.answer: A circle with center J and radius 2 cm (diameter 4 cm).

questions.label: Review 7
questions.q: Draw circles K and O in which their radius = 3 cm and that their circumferences touch each other.
questions.hint: If two circles just touch, how far apart are their centers?
steps: Each radius is 3 cm. Where the circles touch, the two radii join in a straight line.
So the centers are 3 cm + 3 cm = 6 cm apart.
Draw a line 6 cm long. Mark K at one end and O at the other end.
Set the compass to 3 cm. Draw a circle around K, then a circle around O.
questions.answer: Two circles of radius 3 cm with centers K and O 6 cm apart, touching at one point.
questions.why: The centers are 3 cm + 3 cm = 6 cm apart.

1 angle is more than 90° but less than 180°

sections.title: Review: 3D Shapes

learn.title: Unit 8 in one look
learn.html:
🔺 Pyramid: flat base, triangle faces meet at one point.

🍦 Cone: circle base, curved surface, one point.

🥫 Cylinder: 2 circle faces, curved surface.

⚽ Sphere: round like a ball.

A net is the flat shape that folds up into a solid.

questions.label: Review 8 (a)
questions.q: Which of the following is a cone, cylinder, sphere or pyramid? Fill in the blanks. (a)
questions.hint: Look at the faces. Are they flat or curved? Do they meet at one point?
steps: It has a flat base with straight sides and triangle faces that meet at one point (the apex).
questions.why: It has a flat base with straight sides and triangle faces that meet at one point (the apex).

questions.label: Review 8 (b)
questions.q: Which of the following is a cone, cylinder, sphere or pyramid? Fill in the blanks. (b)
questions.hint: Look at the faces. Are they flat or curved? Do they meet at one point?
steps: It has a circle base and a curved surface that comes to one point.
questions.why: It has a circle base and a curved surface that comes to one point.

questions.label: Review 8 (c)
questions.q: Which of the following is a cone, cylinder, sphere or pyramid? Fill in the blanks. (c)
questions.hint: Look at the faces. Are they flat or curved? Do they meet at one point?
steps: It has 2 equal circle faces and a curved surface.
questions.why: It has 2 equal circle faces and a curved surface.

questions.label: Review 8 (d)
questions.q: Which of the following is a cone, cylinder, sphere or pyramid? Fill in the blanks. (d)
questions.hint: Look at the faces. Are they flat or curved? Do they meet at one point?
steps: Its base is a triangle and all the other faces are triangles that meet at one point.
questions.why: Its base is a triangle and all the other faces are triangles that meet at one point.

questions.label: Review 8 (e)
questions.q: Which of the following is a cone, cylinder, sphere or pyramid? Fill in the blanks. (e)
questions.hint: Look at the faces. Are they flat or curved? Do they meet at one point?
steps: It is round like a ball. It has only a curved surface.
questions.why: It is round like a ball. It has only a curved surface.

questions.label: Review 8 (f)
questions.q: Which of the following is a cone, cylinder, sphere or pyramid? Fill in the blanks. (f)
questions.hint: Look at the faces. Are they flat or curved? Do they meet at one point?
steps: Its base has straight sides and the triangle faces meet at one point.
questions.why: Its base has straight sides and the triangle faces meet at one point.

questions.label: Review 9
questions.q: Tick (✓) the solid that can be formed from the given net.
questions.hint: Count the faces in the net. What shape is in the middle?
steps: The net has 1 square in the middle.
It has 4 triangles, one on each side of the square.
Fold up the triangles: they meet at one point on top.
A square base + 4 triangle faces = a square pyramid.
questions.why: 1 square and 4 triangles fold into a square pyramid.

sections.title: Review: Perimeter and Area of Triangles

learn.title: Unit 9 in one look
learn.html:
📏 Perimeter = add all the sides.

🔺 Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.

The height always makes a right angle with the base. Sometimes it is outside the triangle.

Shaded part = whole area - the white parts.

questions.q: Find the perimeter and area of each triangle. (a)
questions.hint: Perimeter = add all 3 sides. Area = ½ × base × height (the height makes a right angle with the base).
steps: All 3 sides are 6 cm. The height on base CB is 5.2 cm.

questions.label: Review 10 (b)

questions.label: Review 10 (d)

steps: The sides are 23 cm, 20 cm and 11 cm. The height on the 11 cm base is 18 cm (it is outside the triangle).

questions.label: Review 12 (b)
questions.q: The figure shows a right triangle. (b) Find the greatest number of such right triangles that can fit into a rectangular piece of cardboard measuring 32 cm by 22 cm.
questions.hint: Two right triangles make a rectangle 6.4 cm by 10.6 cm. How many of those rectangles fit?
steps: Along 32 cm: 6.4 × 5 = 32 cm, so 5 fit in a row.
Along 22 cm: 10.6 × 2 = 21.2 cm, so 2 rows fit (3 rows would be 31.8 cm, too tall).
Each 6.4 cm by 10.6 cm rectangle holds 2 right triangles.

questions.label: Review 13

questions.label: Review 14
questions.q: A triangular tray is of height 20 cm and of base 48 cm. Find the area of this tray.
questions.hint: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.
questions.answer: The area of the tray is 480 cm².

questions.label: Review 15
questions.q: The figure is made up of 2 squares, ABCD and EFGD. AG = 18 cm and CE = ED. ADG is a straight line. Find the area of triangle AEG.
questions.hint: CE = ED, so the small square's side is half of the big square's side. Use units.
steps: The small square EFGD has side ED = 1 unit.
CE = ED, so the big square's side CD = 2 units. So AD = 2 units.
AG = AD + DG = 2 units + 1 unit = 3 units = 18 cm.
Triangle AEG: base AG = 18 cm, height ED = 6 cm.
questions.answer: The area of triangle AEG is 54 cm².
questions.why: 3 units = 18 cm, so 1 unit = 6 cm. ½ × 18 × 6 = 54 cm².

learn.title: Unit 10 in one look
learn.html:
📐 Sum of the interior angles = (number of sides - 2) × 180°.

📏 Perimeter: go all the way round the outside.

Tick marks = equal sides.

🧩 Area: cut the figure into rectangles, squares and triangles, then add (or take away).

questions.hint: All 6 sides are equal (tick marks) and each angle is 120°. Add all 6 angles.
steps: ABCDEF has 6 angles. Each one is 120°.
Check: a 6-sided shape cuts into 4 triangles: 4 × 180° = 720° ✓
questions.answer: The interior angles of ABCDEF add up to 720°.

questions.label: Review 16 (b)

questions.answer: The interior angles of IJKLM add up to 540°.

Sides with 1 tick are both 16.2 cm: BC and CD.

questions.hint: Cut the figure into 2 squares, A and B.

questions.label: Review 18 (b)
questions.q: Find the area of each figure. (All lines meet at right angles.) (b)
questions.hint: HG, FE and DC have tick marks, so they are equal and together make 21 cm. Cut the figure into 3 rectangles.
steps: HG + FE + DC = 21 cm and they are equal: 21 ÷ 3 = 7 cm each.
The heights: AH = 24 cm. The top 2 steps are 7 cm each, so FG = 24 - 7 - 7 = 10 cm.

questions.label: Review 19
questions.q: Joe cut an aluminum sheet into the shape and size as shown below. Find the area of this aluminum sheet. Given that BC = CH = HD = GF, AG = 12 cm and DE = 18 cm.
questions.hint: Start with rectangle ADEF. Take away triangle ABG. Add triangle BCD on top.
steps: GF = AF - AG = 18 - 12 = 6 cm, so BC = CH = HD = 6 cm.
BCHD is a square, so BD = 6 cm too. AB = 20 - 6 = 14 cm.
questions.answer: The area of the aluminum sheet is 294 cm².

learn.title: Unit 11 in one look

⭕ Circumference = 2 × π × radius = π × diameter.

🟡 Area = π × radius × radius.

Half circle = ½ of these. A quarter circle = ¼.

Use the π the question tells you: 22/7 or 3.14.

learn.title: Unit 14 in one look
learn.html:
🥧 Whole circle = 1 = 100%.

Little square = a quarter (1/4 = 25%). Straight line through the centre = halves.

Know one part? Find the total first, then the other parts.

Ratio: write the numbers in the order the question says, then simplify.

questions.label: Review 29 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different types of buns sold by a bakery on Saturday. (a) What was the total percentage of coconut buns, cheese buns and jam buns sold?
questions.hint: Chicken floss buns have a little square: a quarter. The whole circle is 100%.
steps: Chicken floss buns are a quarter: 1/4 = 25%.

questions.label: Review 29 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different types of buns sold by a bakery on Saturday. (b) There were 140 coconut buns sold. How many buns were sold altogether?
questions.hint: Coconut buns are 1/3 of the circle.
steps: Coconut buns = 1/3 of all the buns = 140.

questions.label: Review 29 (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different types of buns sold by a bakery on Saturday. (c) How many chicken floss buns were sold?
questions.hint: Chicken floss buns are 1/4 of all 420 buns.

questions.label: Review 29 (d)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different types of buns sold by a bakery on Saturday. (d) What fraction of the total number of buns sold were cheese buns and jam buns?
questions.hint: The whole is 1. Take away coconut (1/3) and chicken floss (1/4). Use twelfths.

questions.label: Review 29 (e)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the different types of buns sold by a bakery on Saturday. (e) The ratio of the number of jam buns to the number of chicken floss buns sold was 5 : 7. How many jam buns were sold?
questions.hint: Chicken floss buns are 7 units = 105.

questions.label: Review 30 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows how Mr Kumar spent his money in a month. He spent 5 times as much money on rent as on transport. (a) What fraction of his money was spent on rent?
questions.hint: Transport is 1/9. Rent is 5 times as much.

questions.label: Review 30 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows how Mr Kumar spent his money in a month. He spent 5 times as much money on rent as on transport. (b) What fraction of his money was spent on food? Give the answer in the simplest form.
questions.hint: The whole is 1. Take away rent and transport.
steps: Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 3. 3/9 = 1/3

questions.label: Review 31 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the favorite ice cream flavors of a group of students. 150 students like chocolate-flavored ice creams. (a) How many students in all took part in the survey?
questions.hint: Chocolate is half of the circle.
steps: Chocolate = half of the circle = 150 students.

questions.label: Review 31 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the favorite ice cream flavors of a group of students. 150 students like chocolate-flavored ice creams. (b) How many students like strawberry-flavored ice creams?
questions.hint: Strawberry has a little square: it is a quarter of the circle.

questions.label: Review 32 (a)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the favorite types of TV programs of a group of children. (a) What percentage of the children like to watch cartoon?
questions.hint: The whole circle is 100%.

questions.label: Review 32 (b)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the favorite types of TV programs of a group of children. (b) How many times as many children like to watch comedy compared to documentary?
questions.hint: Divide comedy by documentary.

questions.label: Review 32 (c)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the favorite types of TV programs of a group of children. (c) There are 240 children who like to watch cartoon. How many children took part in the survey altogether?
questions.hint: Cartoon is 40% and that is 240 children. Find 1%, then 100%.

questions.label: Review 32 (d)
questions.q: The pie chart shows the favorite types of TV programs of a group of children. (d) What is the ratio of the number of children who like to watch drama to the number of children who like to watch cartoon?
questions.hint: Use the percentages. Drama first, then cartoon. Then simplify.

flash.back: A circle cut into slices to show data. Also called a circle graph.
One part of a pie chart. A bigger amount has a bigger slice.
1/4 = 25%. It has a little square (right angle) at the centre.
1/2 = 50%. A straight line through the centre cuts it in half.
Part ÷ total. Example: 40 boys out of 160 = 40/160 = 1/4.
Total take away all the other slices. Example: 100% - 40% - 20% = 40%.
